prompt:
Create a 3x1 sprite sheet for a modern 16-bit-style pixel-art RPG: one MONSTER in three battle poses.

Image 1 is a LAYOUT GUIDE: three cells on white. In each cell the light-grey box shows where the monster stands and how big it is, the grey line is the ground, and the arrow shows the facing: the monster faces RIGHT, toward the heroes. Draw the SAME monster once in every cell, filling its box. Never draw the grey box, line or arrow.

Image 2 is the HOUSE STYLE: an approved hero sprite sheet from this same game. Match its sprite-pixel size, black outlines, flat shading with 2-3 tones per colour and level of detail exactly, but do NOT copy the hero; it is a different character.

Image 3 is an APPROVED MONSTER sheet from this same game (a DIFFERENT monster, idle | attack | hurt): match its sprite-pixel size, rendering, shading, outline weight and level of detail, and how much the poses move. Do NOT copy that monster's body, colours or equipment.

Render as true pixel art: the monster about 56-72 pixels tall in sprite pixels, every sprite pixel a hard-edged square, no anti-aliasing, no gradients.

Monster: a tall slender regal fish-man with deep indigo-blue scales and a pale silver belly, a flowing cape of long sea-green fins with dark outlines joined to its shoulders and arms, a pearl circlet on its finned head, gold eyes, holding a short curved blade of pink coral in each hand (exactly two blades, one in each hand); centred in its own cell with empty space on both sides. Keep every detail identical in every cell. FACE: its regal fish face with gold eyes under the pearl circlet is readable.

Cells:
- left cell: idle, a ready battle stance facing right.
- middle cell: attack, lunging forward and slashing both coral blades down in front of its chest at the heroes, the elbows bent so the blades stay well inside the middle cell, exactly two blades as in the idle cell, facing right.
- right cell: hurt, knocked back, the head thrown back, both blades flung out to the sides, still one in each hand, recoiling away from the heroes (leaning left), still facing right.

MOVEMENT: the attack and hurt cells are dramatic ACTION frames, not static stances. Use a strong diagonal line of action through the whole body, shift the weight clearly onto one leg, twist the torso and slash the blades with the elbows bent, so every reaching part stays well inside its own cell. The fin cape is part of its body (fins joined to the shoulders and arms) and moves with the motion. Draw only the parts named in the description, the same in every cell: no cloth cape or cloak, and no slash trail, smear or motion lines. Each of the three silhouettes must be clearly different. BODY: in every cell, standing on two feet, both feet on the ground line. No mist, smoke or ground effects.

One monster per cell and nothing else: no props on the ground, no effects outside the monster, no text.
Background: solid flat magenta (#FF00FF) everywhere, no floor, no shadows, no borders.
Avoid: two creatures in one cell, different creatures in different cells, background scenery, floor tiles, shadows on the ground, magic effects outside the cell, text, frame, border, grid lines, blurry, soft shading, gradient, 3d render, a trident, a spear, a shield, armour plates, a cloth cape, a crown, a third blade, an anglerfish lure, magenta, pink fins.
